To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the following are the most important challenges of intercultural communication on global virtual teams: language barriers, cultural differences, and technological problems.

(1) the most important factor for the success of a virtual team is a high degree of trust among team members, and (2) the most important factors in developing trust are communication skills, including active listening, and cultural sensitivity.

the use of a language that is not the mother tongue of the team members is a challenge to global virtual teams, and the challenges that the use of English as a lingua franca (ELF) poses for global virtual teams are: (a) language barriers; (b) cultural barriers; (c) technology barriers; and (d) collaboration barriers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how language, culture, technology, and collaboration affect the communication process of intercultural virtual teams.
the role of language in the construction of identity.
how global virtual teams (GVT) communicate, collaborate, and work together in a virtual environment.

the research study of the intercultural communication of global virtual teams has been a success.

we are a global team that works on the topic of global teams.

The main takeaway from our work is that

we can’t just assume that the way we communicate is the same as the way our customers communicate, and that we can’t assume that the way our customers are communicating with us is the same as how they communicate with each other.

the challenges faced by global virtual teams are not unique to the virtual environment but rather are a reflection of the cultural, language, and technological challenges inherent in global business and international collaboration.
global virtual teams need to be aware of the challenges they face when working in different cultural and linguistic contexts.
